theory.overview: A stack is a linear data structure following the LIFO (Last In, First Out) principle—the last element added is the first to be removed. Think of a stack of plates: you add plates on top and remove from the top. Stacks support two primary operations: push (add to top) and pop (remove from top), both $O(1)$. Stacks are fundamental in computer science, used for function call management (call stack), undo/redo functionality, expression evaluation, backtracking algorithms, and many other applications. This chapter covers stack implementation, applications, and classic stack-based problems.

sections.title: Stack Operations
sections.content: Core operations: push(val) adds to top ($O(1)$), pop() removes and returns top ($O(1)$), peek() returns top without removing ($O(1)$), isEmpty() checks if empty ($O(1)$), size() returns element count ($O(1)$). Implementation can use array (dynamic array with pointer to top) or linked list (head as top). Array implementation is cache-friendly but may need resizing. Linked list has no resizing but poor cache locality. Both achieve $O(1)$ for all operations.

sections.title: Call Stack and Recursion
sections.content: Every function call pushes a stack frame onto the call stack, containing local variables, return address, and parameters. When function returns, frame is popped. This is why recursion works—each recursive call adds a frame, and returns unwind the stack. Stack overflow occurs when stack exceeds its fixed size (typically 1-8 MB), usually from infinite recursion or very deep recursion. Understanding the call stack helps debug recursion depth issues and understand program execution flow.

stackFrame.overflow: Infinite recursion, deep recursion, large local arrays

sections.title: Expression Evaluation
sections.content: Stacks evaluate expressions in correct order. Infix notation (a + b) is human-readable but requires precedence rules. Postfix (Reverse Polish Notation: a b +) and Prefix (Polish Notation: + a b) don't need parentheses or precedence. Postfix evaluation: push operands, when operator encountered, pop required operands, apply operator, push result. Infix to postfix conversion uses operator stack with precedence rules. This is how compilers and calculators evaluate expressions.

notations.description: Operator after operands, easy to evaluate

sections.title: Monotonic Stack
sections.content: Monotonic stack maintains elements in sorted order (increasing or decreasing). Used to find next greater/smaller element in $O(n)$ time. For next greater element: iterate through array, maintain stack of elements in decreasing order. For each element, pop while stack top < current (current is next greater for popped). Push current. Similarly for next smaller element (maintain increasing order). Applications: stock span problem, histogram calculations, finding next greater element in array.
sections.pattern: For next greater: maintain decreasing stack. Pop while top < current. Current is answer for popped. Push current.

sections.title: Common Stack Applications
sections.content: Undo/redo: two stacks—one for actions, one for undone actions. When undo, pop from action stack to undo stack. Redo pops from undo stack. Backtracking: stack stores state to explore alternatives. Parentheses matching: push opening, pop on closing (check match). If stack empty at end, valid. Valid parentheses, HTML/XML validation. Browser history: back button pops from history stack. Depth-First Search: stack (explicit or recursion) for traversal.

applications.name: Parentheses Matching
applications.mechanism: Push open, pop on close, check match

keyConcepts.name: LIFO Principle
keyConcepts.description: Last In, First Out. Most recently added element is removed first. Analogy: stack of plates, browser back button.
keyConcepts.implication: Access only to top element, no random access

keyConcepts.name: Amortized Analysis
keyConcepts.description: Array-based stack occasionally resizes (O(n) copy), but average push is O(1). n pushes cost O(n) total.
keyConcepts.math: Total cost for n operations: O(n), Amortized: O(1) per operation

keyConcepts.name: Stack Overflow
keyConcepts.description: Exceeding stack size limit. Causes program crash. Common causes: infinite recursion, very deep recursion, large local variables.
keyConcepts.prevention: Increase stack size, use iteration instead of recursion, limit recursion depth

keyConcepts.name: Monotonicity
keyConcepts.description: Stack maintains elements in sorted order. Enables O(n) solutions for problems that would be O(n²) naive.
keyConcepts.pattern: Pop while condition violated, push current, record answer during pop

steps.title: Initialize Stack
steps.description: Create empty stack with underlying array or linked list.
steps.code: Stack stack = new Stack(); // top = -1 for array

steps.title: Push Element
steps.description: Increment top pointer, add element at top position.

steps.title: Peek Top
steps.description: Return element at top position without removing.

steps.title: Pop Element
steps.description: Return element at top, decrement top pointer.

practiceProblems.title: Valid Parentheses
practiceProblems.description: Given string with '(){}[]', determine if valid (every opening has matching closing in correct order).
practiceProblems.example: Input: '()[]{}'. Output: true. Input: '(]'. Output: false
practiceProblems.solution: Stack for opening brackets. For each char: if opening, push. If closing, check if stack top matches. If empty or no match, invalid. At end, stack must be empty.
hints: On closing, check stack top matches
Stack must be empty at end

practiceProblems.title: Min Stack
practiceProblems.description: Implement stack with push, pop, and getMin in O(1) time.
practiceProblems.solution: Two stacks: main stack and min stack. On push: push to main, push to min if ≤ min.top. On pop: pop from both if top values equal. getMin returns min.top.
hints: Push to min only if ≤ current min
Pop from both if values equal

practiceProblems.title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
practiceProblems.description: Evaluate postfix expression (operators after operands).
practiceProblems.solution: Stack for operands. For each token: if number, push. If operator, pop two operands, apply, push result. Final result is stack top.
hints: On operator, pop two, apply, push result

practiceProblems.title: Valid Parentheses with Star
practiceProblems.description: String with '(', ')', '*' (can be '(' or ')' or empty). Determine if valid.
practiceProblems.solution: Two stacks: one for '(' indices, one for '*' indices. On ')': pop '(' if exists, else pop '*'. At end: match remaining '(' with stars after them.

practiceProblems.title: Simplify Path
practiceProblems.description: Simplify Unix-style file path (resolve '.' and '..').
practiceProblems.solution: Split by '/'. Use stack: skip '.' and empty. On '..' pop if not empty. Push other directories. Join with '/'.

practiceProblems.title: Next Greater Element I
practiceProblems.description: For each element in nums1, find next greater element in nums2.
practiceProblems.solution: Hash map for nums2 elements to their next greater. Use monotonic decreasing stack on nums2. For each element, pop while stack top < current (current is next greater). Store in map.
hints: Store next greater in hash map

practiceProblems.title: Next Greater Element II
practiceProblems.description: Find next greater element for each element in circular array.
practiceProblems.solution: Traverse array twice (2n iterations). Monotonic decreasing stack. For each element, pop while stack top < current. Store answer. Push index.

practiceProblems.title: Daily Temperatures
practiceProblems.description: Given daily temperatures, return array of days until warmer temperature.
practiceProblems.solution: Monotonic decreasing stack of indices. For each day, pop while temperature[stack.top] < current. Answer for popped = current index - popped index.

practiceProblems.title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
practiceProblems.description: Find largest rectangular area in histogram.
practiceProblems.solution: Monotonic increasing stack of indices. For each bar, pop while height[top] < current. Area with popped bar as height = height[popped] × (current index - stack.top - 1). Append sentinel 0 at end.
hints: When smaller bar, calculate area with popped bars

practiceProblems.title: Trapping Rain Water
practiceProblems.description: Calculate how much water can be trapped after raining given elevation map.
practiceProblems.solution: Two stacks: one for left max, one for right max. Or monotonic stack: push indices, when current height > stack.top, pop and calculate water trapped at that index.
hints: When taller bar found, calculate trapped water
Water at index = min(left_max, right_max) - height[i]

practiceProblems.title: Basic Calculator II
practiceProblems.description: Evaluate expression with +, -, *, / (no parentheses).
practiceProblems.solution: Stack for numbers. Parse number, check operator before it. If + or -, push number (with sign). If * or /, pop, compute, push result. Sum stack at end.
hints: + and - can be delayed to end

practiceProblems.title: Remove All Adjacent Duplicates
practiceProblems.description: Remove adjacent duplicates repeatedly.
practiceProblems.solution: Stack. For each char: if stack not empty and top == char, pop. Else push char. Result is stack contents.
hints: If top equals current, pop (remove duplicate)

practiceProblems.title: Remove K Digits
practiceProblems.description: Remove k digits to make smallest possible number.
practiceProblems.solution: Monotonic increasing stack. For each digit: while k>0 and stack top > digit, pop, k--. Push digit. After loop, remove k more from end (if any). Remove leading zeros.
hints: Pop while top > current (to make smaller)
Remove remaining k from end, strip leading zeros

practiceProblems.title: Find Celebrity
practiceProblems.description: Find celebrity (everyone knows them, they know no one) using minimal calls.
practiceProblems.solution: Stack approach: push all. While stack > 1: pop two, if a knows b, a not celebrity (push b). Else b not celebrity (push a). Verify candidate knows no one and everyone knows them.
hints: If a knows b, a not celebrity

practiceProblems.title: Decode String
practiceProblems.description: Decode string like '3[a]2[bc]' to 'aaabcbc'. Nested patterns allowed.
practiceProblems.solution: Two stacks: one for counts, one for strings. On digit: build number. On '[': push count and current string, reset. On ']': pop count and string, repeat current string count times, prepend to popped string.

practiceProblems.title: Score of Parentheses
practiceProblems.description: Calculate score of balanced parentheses: '()' = 1, '(A)' = 2*score(A), 'AB' = score(A) + score(B).
practiceProblems.solution: Stack of scores. Push 0 for '('. On ')': pop, if top is 0, push 1. Else: pop, multiply by 2, push result. Sum consecutive scores.

practiceProblems.title: Backspace String Compare
practiceProblems.description: Compare two strings after processing backspace characters ('#').
practiceProblems.solution: Stack for each string. For each char: if '#', pop if not empty. Else push char. Compare both stacks. Or build strings by processing backwards.

practiceProblems.title: Implement Queue using Stacks
practiceProblems.description: Implement queue using two stacks (push efficient or pop efficient).
practiceProblems.solution: Two stacks: input and output. Push: push to input. Pop/peek: if output empty, move all from input to output. Then pop/peek from output.
hints: Pop/peek from output, refill from input if empty

practiceProblems.title: Implement Stack using Queues
practiceProblems.description: Implement stack using one or two queues.
practiceProblems.solution: Two queues. Push: enqueue to q2, move all from q1 to q2, swap q1 and q2. Pop/peek: dequeue from q1. Each push is O(n) due to moving elements.
hints: Push: add to empty queue, move all, swap

practiceProblems.title: Asteroid Collision
practiceProblems.description: Given asteroids moving in line, collisions destroy smaller (equal destroys both).
practiceProblems.solution: Stack. For each asteroid: if positive, push. If negative, while stack positive and top < abs(current): pop. If stack empty or top negative: push. If equal: pop (both destroyed).

practiceProblems.title: Online Stock Span
practiceProblems.description: Calculate stock span (consecutive days with price ≤ current) for each day.
practiceProblems.solution: Monotonic decreasing stack of (price, span). For each price: pop while price ≥ stack.top.price. Span = current index - stack.top.index. Push (price, span).
hints: Span = current index - previous greater index

practiceProblems.title: Maximal Rectangle
practiceProblems.description: Find largest rectangle containing only 1s in binary matrix.
practiceProblems.solution: Treat each row as histogram base. For each row, update heights (heights[j] = 0 if matrix[i][j] == 0 else heights[j] + 1). Use histogram max rectangle algorithm (monotonic stack) on each row.
hints: Apply histogram algorithm for each row

practiceProblems.title: Sliding Window Maximum
practiceProblems.description: Find max in each sliding window of size k.
practiceProblems.solution: Monotonic decreasing deque (double-ended queue). Store indices. Remove indices outside window. Remove from back while values ≤ current. Push current. Front is max.

practiceProblems.title: Binary Tree Inorder Traversal
practiceProblems.description: Iterative inorder traversal using stack (no recursion).
practiceProblems.solution: Stack. Push all left nodes. Pop, visit, move to right, push all left of right. Repeat until stack empty and current null.
hints: After visiting, go to right subtree

practiceProblems.title: Validate Stack Sequences
practiceProblems.description: Given pushed and popped sequences, determine if valid.
practiceProblems.solution: Simulate with stack. Iterate through pushed, push each. While stack top equals popped[current], pop and advance popped. At end, stack should be empty.

minigame.description: Test your stack skills! Push, pop, and solve stack-based puzzles against the clock.
